title: The Use of Nerve Blocks and Ongoing Pressure Monitoring for Tibia Fracture Management
official: Regional Anesthesia With Continuous Intracompartmental Pressure Monitoring in Tibia Shaft and Plateau Fractures: A Prospective Pilot Feasibility Study
summary: This study will assess whether regional anesthesia treatment combined with continuous pressure monitoring can safely control pain in patients having surgery for certain types of broken-leg fractures. A medical device, known as the MY01 Continuous Compartmental Pressure Monitor, will continuously monitor pressure in the leg muscle for up to 48 hours after surgery to help detect acute compartment syndrome (ACS), a serious complication. Hospital personnel will regularly examine the patient's fractured leg, assess pain, and ask the patient how satisfied they are with their pain relief.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults, 18 years of age or older
* Closed tibial shaft or plateau fracture
* Operative fixation and regional anesthesia treatment planned at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
* Planned admission to Cedars-Sinai Medical Center for a minimum of 24 hours
* Able to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Suspected acute compartment syndrome (ACS) requiring an emergency procedure known as a fasciotomy
* Open contaminated fractures
* Medical history that includes any of the following conditions: peripheral neuropathy, vascular disease, or other neurovascular conditions affecting the study limb
* Pregnant or lactating women
* Unable to participate in serial neurovascular exams
* Bilateral tibia fractures
